{{Short description|Taiwanese biologist}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Wu (surname)|Wu]]|lang=Chinese}}

'''Chung-I Wu''' ({{zh|s=吴仲义|t=吳仲義}}; born 1954) is a Taiwanese biologist, academician of Academia Sinica, and former professor at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chung-I Wu {{!}} Committee on Evolutionary Biology |url=https://evbio.uchicago.edu/program/faculty/chung-i-wu |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=evbio.uchicago.edu}}</ref> He was also the second director of the Beijing Genomics Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=历任所长----中国科学院北京基因组研究所 |url=http://www.big.ac.cn/gkjj/lrld/ |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=www.big.ac.cn}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Wu has received awards throughout his career, including the NIH Research Career Development Award from 1990 to 1995,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wu |first=Chung-I. |title=Molecular/Evolutionary Genetics of Segregation Distortio |url=https://grantome.com/grant/NIH/K04-HG000005-02 |language=en}}</ref> the Down Syndrome Foundation Award from 1989 to 1991,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Admin1 |date=2018-02-19 |title=2034. Prof. Chung-I Wu 吳仲義教授 |url=https://taiwaneseamericanhistory.org/blog/whos-who-2034-chung-i-wu/ |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=History of Taiwanese American (T.A. Archives) 台美史料中心 |language=en-US}}</ref> AAAS fellow in 2004,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chung-I Wu {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |url=https://www.aaas.org/person/chung-i-wu |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=www.aaas.org |language=en}}</ref> and the Outstanding Alumnus Award from [[Tunghai University]] in 2004. In 2004, he was also elected as an academician of Academia Sinica.<ref>{{Cite web |title=院士簡歷 |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n/show&id=139 |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=academicians.sinica.edu.tw}}</ref>

== Scientific studies ==
Chung-I Wu has made numerous contributions in the field of [[molecular evolution]], population genetics, and evolutionary genomics, particularly in the genetic basis of speciation and natural selection. He pioneered the study of speciation at the molecular level,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wu |first=Chung-I |date=January 1985 |title=A Stochastic Simulation Study on Speciation by Sexual Selection |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2307/2408517 |journal=Evolution |volume=39 |issue=1 |pages=66 |doi=10.2307/2408517 |issn=0014-3820|url-access=subscription }}</ref> introducing cutting-edge gene replacement techniques to answer classical ecological questions in the model organism Drosophila.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Johnson |first=N A |last2=Hollocher |first2=H |last3=Noonburg |first3=E |last4=Wu |first4=C I |date=1993-10-01 |title=The effects of interspecific Y chromosome replacements on hybrid sterility within the Drosophila simulans clade. |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1093/genetics/135.2.443 |journal=Genetics |volume=135 |issue=2 |pages=443–453 |doi=10.1093/genetics/135.2.443 |issn=1943-2631|pmc=1205647 }}</ref> He also made original contributions in areas such as selfish genes,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Werren |first=John H. |last2=Nur |first2=Uzi |last3=Wu |first3=Chung-I |date=1988-11-01 |title=Selfish genetic elements |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/016953478890105X |journal=Trends in Ecology & Evolution |language=en |volume=3 |issue=11 |pages=297–302 |doi=10.1016/0169-5347(88)90105-X |issn=0169-5347|url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref> molecular clocks,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=January 1988 |title=Molecular evolution of intergenic DNA in higher primates: pattern of DNA changes, molecular clock, and evolution of repetitive sequences. |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a040479 |journal=Molecular Biology and Evolution |doi=10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a040479 |issn=1537-1719|doi-access=free }}</ref> X chromosome degeneration, and evolutionary genomics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zimmer |first=Carl |date=2013-05-18 |title=狗是如何进化为人类的好朋友的 |url=https://cn.nytimes.com/science/20130516/c17dogs/ |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=New York times (纽约时报中文网) |language=zh-cmn-hans}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Zimmer |first=Carl |date=2013-05-16 |title=From Fearsome Predator to Man’s Best Friend |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/05/16/science/dogs-from-fearsome-predator-to-mans-best-friend.html |access-date=2023-04-04 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> His proposed hypotheses on the genetic mechanism of reproductive isolation and the gene concept of speciation are innovative and represent a significant departure from traditional ideas in species biology. He has published over 130 papers in top international journals such as Science, Nature, and PNAS, with 14 papers as corresponding author in Science, Nature, and Cell. In 2011, he received the second prize of the National Natural Science Award. He is currently the section editor of National Science Review.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editorial_Board |url=https://academic.oup.com/nsr/pages/Editorial_Board |access-date=2023-04-04 |website=Oxford Academic |language=en}}</ref>
